newsitem.title: GERMANY: BUNDS REBOUND FROM LOSSES AS RATE FEARS RECEDE.
newsitem.headline: BUNDS REBOUND FROM LOSSES AS RATE FEARS RECEDE.

text.p: German Bunds were moderately firmer in mid-morning trade Thursday after recovering from early losses after the Bundesbank denied market rumours it planned to make a statement or hold a news conference.
September Bunds were quoted at 101.96 at 0750 GMT, down four basis points from Wednesday's close, after slipping as low as 101.83 earlier in the session.

Bunds had closed firmer on Wednesday as fears receded of an interest rate rise by the Bundesbank in defence of the mark. But they came under pressure again early on Thursday on rumours the Bundesbank was planning to make a statement.
The bank's prompt denial helped push the dollar down against the mark to 1.8820 marks from 1.8860 marks, and took pressure off the short end of the market, dealers said.
The dollar/mark rate will remain the market's main focus today. "If the dollar goes above 1.89 we could see Bunds sliding to 101.50," one Frankfurt-based dealer said.
Frankfurt dealers said they doubted that the Bundesbank would make any announcement on the repo rate before next Tuesday, when its sets the repo tender for next week.
Traders speculated this week that the bank might pave the way for higher money market rates in defence of the mark.

The Bundesbank's last central bank council meeting before its one-month summer break on July 24 took the unusual step of setting fixed-rate repo tenders for just two weeks, even though the council was only due to reconvene after four weeks.

The second of those weekly repo pacts was allocated on Wednesday, leaving markets in the dark as to whether next week's repo tender will be a fixed-rate repo at 3.00 percent, a variable-rate repo, or a fixed-rate repo at a higher rate.
Theoretically, the Bundesbank does not have to say what form the tender will take until it invites bids from banks for repos next Tuesday.
But with markets speculating feverishly about whether the Bundesbank will shift to higher rates, dealers had speculated the bank may make an announcement sooner.
